lede: A rope that pulls at an angle is doing two jobs at once: dragging along the floor and lifting. Resolving splits one slanted force into those two straight ones, so the rest of the mechanics can be done a direction at a time.
can: Split a force at an angle into a component along a line and one at right angles to it
Resolve the weight of a body on a slope into its two components
Read which angle to use, and which line it is measured from

md: Pull a suitcase by its handle and it goes forwards, but the handle is tilted, so some of your pull is lifting it rather than dragging it. Splitting that one pull into a forwards part and an upwards part is what resolving does.

alt: A force of 42 N drawn as an arrow at 28 degrees above a horizontal line. Dashed lines complete a right-angled triangle: the side along the floor is labelled 42 cos 28 degrees and the side at right angles to it is labelled 42 sin 28 degrees.
svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 325 143' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='325' height='143'><g fill='currentColor' font-family='inherit'><path d='M28 102.4L242.4 102.4' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='242.4' y='122.4' text-anchor='end' font-size='11.5'>the floor</text><path d='M190.4 102.4L190.4 32' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='5 4' stroke-opacity='0.75'/><path d='M58 102.4L190.4 102.4' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='5 4' stroke-opacity='0.75'/><path d='M180.4 102.4L180.4 92.4L190.4 92.4' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='0.9' stroke-opacity='0.7'/><path d='M58 102.4L190.4 32' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.9' stroke-opacity='1'/><path d='M190.4 32L184.3 39.6L180.7 32.9Z' fill='currentColor'/><text x='196.6' y='23.7' text-anchor='start' font-size='12.5' font-weight='600'>42 N</text><path d='M100 102.4A42 42 0 0 0 95.1 82.7' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-opacity='0.85'/><text x='114.3' y='92.4' text-anchor='middle' font-size='12'>28°</text><text x='124.2' y='122.4' text-anchor='middle' font-size='12'>42 cos 28°</text><text x='198.4' y='71.2' text-anchor='start' font-size='12'>42 sin 28°</text></g></svg>
caption: One slanted force replaced by two at right angles.

md:
Drop a dashed line from the tip of the force arrow onto the line you care about. The force is now the longest side of a right-angled triangle, and the two shorter sides are its components.

The side beside the angle is the one along the line, so it uses cosine: $42\cos 28° = 37.08$ N. The side opposite uses sine: $42\sin 28° = 19.72$ N.

prompt: In the triangle above, a rope pulls with a force of 42 N at 28° to the floor. Which expression gives the part of the pull that drags along the floor?
explain: The floor is the side next to the $28°$ angle, and the side next to the angle is the cosine one.

text: 2. Cosine goes with the angle you are given

alt: A two-column table. The component along a line is F multiplied by the cosine of the angle between the force and that line. The component at right angles to it is F multiplied by the sine of the same angle. On a slope of angle a the weight gives mg sine a down the slope and mg cosine a into it.
svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 548 210' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='548' height='210'><g fill='currentColor' font-family='inherit'><rect x='2' y='2' width='544' height='206' rx='8' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1' stroke-opacity='0.5'/><text x='12' y='35' text-anchor='start' font-size='13.5' font-weight='600'>Resolving one force</text><text x='12' y='65' text-anchor='start' font-size='12' font-weight='600'>Component</text><text x='206' y='65' text-anchor='start' font-size='12' font-weight='600'>How it is worked out</text><text x='12' y='95' text-anchor='start' font-size='13'>along the line</text><text x='206' y='95' text-anchor='start' font-size='13'>F cos of the angle between F and the line</text><text x='12' y='125' text-anchor='start' font-size='13'>at right angles to it</text><text x='206' y='125' text-anchor='start' font-size='13'>F sin of that same angle</text><text x='12' y='155' text-anchor='start' font-size='13'>down a slope of angle a</text><text x='206' y='155' text-anchor='start' font-size='13'>mg sin a</text><text x='12' y='185' text-anchor='start' font-size='13'>into a slope of angle a</text><text x='206' y='185' text-anchor='start' font-size='13'>mg cos a</text><path d='M6 76H542M6 106H542M6 136H542M6 166H542M6 196H542M200 46V196' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='0.8' stroke-opacity='0.45'/></g></svg>
caption: The same two lines, whichever direction you are resolving along.

md:
Write it once and it is yours: the component **along** a line is $F\cos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between the force and that line; the component **at right angles** is $F\sin\theta$.

Everything hangs on which angle $\theta$ is, so mark it on the diagram before reaching for the calculator.

title: Why cosine shortens the force
md: Think of the arrow's shadow on the line. When the force lies along the line there is no tilt, $\cos 0° = 1$, and the whole force counts. Turn it to a right angle and the shadow vanishes, which is $\cos 90° = 0$. Cosine is the fraction of the force that survives the turn.

prompt: A force of 20 N acts at 60° to a straight line. What is its component along that line, in newtons?
explain: $20\cos 60° = 20 \times 0.5 = 10$ N. Half the force survives a turn of $60°$.

text: 3. The weight of a body on a slope

alt: A box of mass 9 kg on a slope inclined at 24 degrees. A solid arrow from the box points straight down and is labelled 90 N. Two dashed arrows split it: one down the slope labelled 90 sin 24 degrees and one into the slope labelled 90 cos 24 degrees.
svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 409 219' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='409' height='219'><g fill='currentColor' font-family='inherit'><path d='M42.6 178.2L376 29.8L376 178.2Z' fill='currentColor' fill-opacity='0.07' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.5'/><path d='M54.6 187.2l8 -9M70.6 187.2l8 -9M86.6 187.2l8 -9M102.6 187.2l8 -9M118.6 187.2l8 -9M134.6 187.2l8 -9M150.6 187.2l8 -9M166.6 187.2l8 -9M182.6 187.2l8 -9M198.6 187.2l8 -9M214.6 187.2l8 -9M230.6 187.2l8 -9M246.6 187.2l8 -9M262.6 187.2l8 -9M278.6 187.2l8 -9M294.6 187.2l8 -9M310.6 187.2l8 -9M326.6 187.2l8 -9M342.6 187.2l8 -9M358.6 187.2l8 -9' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='0.8' stroke-opacity='0.45'/><path d='M76.6 178.2A34 34 0 0 0 73.6 164.4' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-opacity='0.85'/><text x='84.6' y='169.2' text-anchor='start' font-size='12'>24°</text><path d='M198.7 71.5L251.7 47.9L265.5 79L212.5 102.6Z' fill='currentColor' fill-opacity='0.12' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='232.1' y='79.3' text-anchor='middle' font-size='12'>9 kg</text><path d='M232.1 93.9L232.1 153.3' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.9' stroke-opacity='1'/><path d='M232.1 153.3L228.3 144.3L235.9 144.3Z' fill='currentColor'/><text x='239.1' y='157.3' text-anchor='start' font-size='12.5' font-weight='600'>90 N</text><path d='M205.6 87L190.1 94' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='5 4' stroke-opacity='0.75'/><path d='M190.1 94L195.3 88.4L197.7 93.8Z' fill='currentColor'/><text x='183.7' y='108.8' text-anchor='end' font-size='12.5'>90 sin 24°</text><path d='M239 90.8L250.8 117.3' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='5 4' stroke-opacity='0.75'/><path d='M250.8 117.3L245.3 112.1L250.6 109.7Z' fill='currentColor'/><text x='253.6' y='135.7' text-anchor='start' font-size='12.5'>90 cos 24°</text></g></svg>
caption: The weight split along the slope and into it.

md:
On a slope the useful directions are along the surface and at right angles to it, so the weight is the force that has to be split.

The angle between the weight and the line into the slope is the slope's own angle $\alpha$. So the component into the slope is $mg\cos\alpha$, and the one left over, down the slope, is $mg\sin\alpha$. Here $90\sin 24° = 36.61$ N and $90\cos 24° = 82.22$ N.

prompt: A box of weight $W$ rests on a slope inclined at $\alpha$ to the horizontal. Which expression gives the component of the weight acting down the slope?
explain: The slope's angle sits between the weight and the line into the surface, so the cosine part goes into the slope and the sine part runs down it.

text: 4. Which line is the angle measured from

alt: A slope drawn at 21 degrees to the page, with a 75 N arrow leaving it at 32 degrees to the slope itself. Dashed lines give a component of 75 cos 32 degrees along the slope and 75 sin 32 degrees at right angles to it.
svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 308 192' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='308' height='192'><g fill='currentColor' font-family='inherit'><path d='M30 162.5L225.3 87.6' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='230.3' y='120.6' text-anchor='end' font-size='11.5'>the slope</text><path d='M176.8 106.2L148.3 32' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='5 4' stroke-opacity='0.75'/><path d='M58 151.8L176.8 106.2' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-dasharray='5 4' stroke-opacity='0.75'/><path d='M167.4 109.8L163.8 100.5L173.2 96.9' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='0.9' stroke-opacity='0.7'/><path d='M58 151.8L148.3 32' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.9' stroke-opacity='1'/><path d='M148.3 32L145.9 41.5L139.8 36.9Z' fill='currentColor'/><text x='152.5' y='21.4' text-anchor='start' font-size='12.5' font-weight='600'>75 N</text><path d='M97.2 136.7A42 42 0 0 0 83.3 118.3' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-opacity='0.85'/><text x='104.3' y='120.9' text-anchor='middle' font-size='12'>32°</text><text x='118.8' y='152.7' text-anchor='middle' font-size='12'>75 cos 32°</text><text x='165.6' y='69.5' text-anchor='start' font-size='12'>75 sin 32°</text></g></svg>
caption: An angle given to the slope, not to the horizontal.

md:
A question may give the angle to the horizontal, to the vertical, or to the slope itself. Only the angle between the force and the direction you are resolving along belongs in the cosine.

Here the rope is $32°$ from the slope, so the component along the slope is $75\cos 32° = 63.60$ N. Taking $32°$ from the horizontal instead would resolve along the wrong line.

title: Mechanics FM GCSE - Resolving Forces on Horizontal plane
why: Taught straight against this specification. Watch the angle being marked on the diagram before either ratio is chosen.

prompt: A rope pulls a box up a slope. The rope is at 32° to the slope, and the slope is at 21° to the horizontal. Which angle is used for the component of the pull along the slope?
explain: The component along the slope needs the angle between the rope and the slope, which the question gives directly as $32°$.

text: 5. Which way does a component point

alt: A point O pulled by a 30 N force acting horizontally to the right and a 20 N force acting up and to the left at 60 degrees to the horizontal, with dashed reference lines through O.
svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 360 205' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' width='360' height='205'><g fill='currentColor' font-family='inherit'><path d='M12 106.7H184M98 20.7V192.7' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='0.9' stroke-dasharray='4 4' stroke-opacity='0.45'/><path d='M98 106.7L180 106.7' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.9' stroke-opacity='1'/><path d='M180 106.7L171 110.5L171 102.9Z' fill='currentColor'/><text x='187' y='110.7' text-anchor='start' font-size='12.5' font-weight='600'>30 N</text><path d='M98 106.7L57 35.7' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.9' stroke-opacity='1'/><path d='M57 35.7L64.8 41.6L58.2 45.4Z' fill='currentColor'/><text x='53.5' y='24.6' text-anchor='end' font-size='12.5' font-weight='600'>20 N</text><path d='M62 106.7A36 36 0 0 1 80 75.5' fill='none' stroke='currentColor' stroke-width='1.2' stroke-opacity='0.85'/><text x='53.8' y='85.2' text-anchor='middle' font-size='11.5'>60°</text><circle cx='98' cy='106.7' r='4.5' fill='currentColor'/><text x='89' y='124.7' text-anchor='end' font-size='12.5' font-weight='600'>O</text></g></svg>
caption: Two pulls whose horizontal parts face each other.

md:
A component has a direction as well as a size. Choose one way along the line as positive, then a component pointing the other way is subtracted rather than added.

With a $30$ N pull to the right and a $20$ N pull at $60°$ above the horizontal but to the left, the total to the right is $30 - 20\cos 60° = 20$ N, not $40$ N.

prompt: A point is pulled by 24 N to the right and by 16 N acting at 60° above the horizontal, to the left. What is the total component to the right, in newtons?
explain: $16\cos 60° = 8$ N to the left, so the total is $24 - 8 = 16$ N. Adding would count the second pull as helping the first.

md:
Split any force into a component along a line and one at right angles to it.
Resolve the weight of a body on a slope into mg sine and mg cosine of the slope's angle.
Pick out which angle the question gives, and which line it is measured from.
Combine components that point opposite ways by subtracting rather than adding.

Resolving is rarely asked for on its own: it sits inside 'Calculate the normal reaction' or 'Calculate the value of P', worth 2 to 4 marks. The first mark is for a correct resolved component written down; the last is for the value, to 2 decimal places. Stuck? Draw the right-angled triangle, mark the angle, and ask which side of it you want.
